newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA'S AGRIBANK IN TALKS WITH FOREIGN INVESTOR.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA'S AGRIBANK IN TALKS WITH FOREIGN INVESTOR.

text.p: Bulgaria's Bank for Agricultural Credit (BAC) is in talks with a potential foreign buyer in a bid to avoid bankruptcy, BAC's executive director Yonka Kinova said on Tuesday.

"A holding structure based in London is interested to acquire the Bank for Agricultural Credit. If they agree with the central bank shortly, the bank will be able to re-open in June," Kinova told reporters, declining to elaborate.
The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) took over 51.9 percent of BAC's voting shares for free last March in bid to preserve bank's depositors interests.
Non-performing loans extended by BAC to its share-holding companies two years ago caused a severe liquidity crisis.
Loans to individuals and companies stood at 67.8 billion levs in December of which 66.3 billion levs were credits denominated in foreign currency.
BAC had collected 20.6 billion levs in principal and interest of its loans since last year, after the BNB appointed a new management team, Kinova said.
Bank assets stood at 74.2 billion levs at the end of 1996. As of April the BAC capital-to risks assets ratio stood at minus 16.82 percent up from minus 40.01 percent at the end of 1996.
The bank's liabilities to companies and individuals in national and foreign currency totalled some 22 billion levs on December 30.
On January 24 the BNB filed an insolvency suit against BAC.
"The BNB had assured BAC that it will withdraw its claim if a strategic investor boosted its liguidity and improved its capital-to-risk assets ratio," Kinova said.
The 1996 auditors report said that BAC was unlikely to operate without capital support and restructuring of its credit portfolio.
The Bank Consolidation Company, which manages state equity in local commercial banks, holds 25.10 percent of BAC's voting shares.
According to BNB preliminary estimates a $20 million investment is needed to strengthen BAC's liquidity and to back payments on due liabilities.
BAC debts to the BNB totalled some 22.6 billion levs including 8.6 billion levs pricipal and some 14 billion levs interests as of April 30, the BAC figures showed.
On May 15 the Sofia City Court postponed ruling on the BAC insolvency case until July 11. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-981-4145
